title: Fughetta in D minor
brief: Baroque-style miniature for harpsichord and strings, about two minutes: a fughetta whose subject each voice takes up in turn, an episode travelling to F major, a harpsichord solo episode to G minor, a dominant pedal with stretto, and a firm cadence with a Picardy third.

sections.intent: Subject in Violin I, answer in Violin II, subject in viola, answer in cello; continuo joins with the bass; cadence in D minor
Descending-fifths sequence with interlocking 7-6 suspensions in the violins; travels to F major
Harpsichord takes the subject in F major, then the cello; lighter texture
Harpsichord solo figuration on a fifths sequence, strings rejoin with suspensions; to G minor
Viola subject in G minor, then a short episode back toward D minor
Dominant pedal; stretto of the subject in the violins; the high point at bar 29
Subject in the bass (cello with harpsichord), full texture, cadential trill, perfect cadence
Tonic pedal with the subject head in viola and Violin II; V7-I to D major

decisions: Chamber forces: one player per string part (solo violin VSCO, Iowa violin and viola, Big Cat cello) and harpsichord continuo, as in a trio-sonata or chamber-concerto fugue.
Harpsichord registration changes for contrast: Flemish 8' for continuo, 8'+4' for its subject entry and solo episode.
c80_db +6: counterpoint for a small ensemble whose lines must be followed (orchestration.md), between the guide's starting sends and a concert hall.
Wide dynamics: no bus compression; the shape comes from texture and the written dynamic plan.
